Answer: D
Reason: The CT images demonstrate a hyperdense, calcified structure (measuring ~425 HU) within the right lower lobe bronchus, which is characteristic of a foreign body (such as an aspirated tooth or bone). This obstruction has led to progressive atelectasis (collapse) of the distal lung parenchyma, distinguishing it from mucous plugging which would typically have soft-tissue density.
